title.narrative: 1.3. Number of parliamentary support activities and initiatives that EU Delegations undertake

description.narrative: Management Purpose: This indicator will measure if one of the projects desired outcomes, for EUDs commit to dedicate separate bilateral funding to support parliamentary development / parliaments. Enhancing the number of EU support projects is taken as a demonstration that the field of Parliamentary Development is growing in importance. Information will be used during implementation to monitor progress and make any necessary changes and the data will also be used to assess the achievement of the outcomes regarding enhancing EU engagement with parliamentary development. Precise Definition of terms: Parliamentary Support initiatives may include any bilateral (nonINTER PARES) program with a parliament whose focus is some aspect of parliamentary capacity development. A single EUD activity carried out with Parliament representative or in support of parliamentary strengthening may also be counted. Initiatives related to the thematic areas and parliamentary functions will be counted. Only activities and interventions that started during this contract (after January 2023) will be counted for this Phase II indicator (however the project may collect information on activities / initiatives starting in 2019 and report these in narrative analysis to get a full picture of INTER PARES outcomes regarding EUD support for parliamentary strengthening). Unit of Measure: number (integer) of activities and initiatives Disaggregated by: None required however for learning and reporting purposes the project will collect data on the EUD country, and whether the initiative/activity occurred before or after January 2023 (start of this contract)Known Data Limitations: None Data Source and Plan for Collection: Data will be gathered through the mapping of the EU support to parliaments worldwide (under activity 1.3.2) and an end of year Survey EoY EU Delegations and EU Partners. The survey would ask EUDs if they did activities or initiatives and when these started. Since the beginning of INTER PARES (January 2019) have you or has your delegation undertaken any parliamentary support activities and/ or initiatives? *a)Activity (undertaking a oneoff event/activity that involves parliament) * Yes No Not sure.b)Initiative (requesting funding for or undertaking a parliamentary capacity development project) * Yes No Not sure.c)When did the initiative start? Method of Data Collection and Construction: Annual countbased feedback received on the mapping and surveys and any End of year interviews with EUDs.Person responsible for the data: Project team and M&E team will develop the surveys, M&E team will prepare survey monkey analysis, Data will be verified by separate project or M&E team person doing data verification.Baseline / Timeframe: The baseline will be established with the results of activity 1.3.2. Mapping of the EU support to parliaments worldwide. Support to parliaments resulting from the projects activities in Phase I will also be counted.

title.narrative: 1.1.Percentage of core institutional partners (CoP members, EUMSPs, EUD) responding to a questionnaire who state that INTER PARES activities have been effective in strengthening parliamentary development

description.narrative: Management Purpose Definition: This indicator aims to determine if the INTER PARES institutional partners perceive that the projects efforts are effective in strengthening the field of parliamentary development. At the end of each year, the projects core partners will be surveyed and asked to reflect on whether project activities delivered in INTER PARES Phase II are contributing positively to the field of parliamentary development. Collecting data from a wide range of partners who are both experts in the field and who have had participated in or observed activities that aim to strengthen parliamentary development will provide feedback regarding the effectiveness of interventions. Information will be used during implementation to monitor progress and make any necessary changes and the data will also be used to assess the achievement of the outcomes regarding partner perceptions of the projects impact.Precise definitions of terms: Core partners refers to individuals collaborating with INTER PARES on Outcome 1 activities. They may be EUMSP staff and MPs, partner parliament staff and MPs involved in Outcome 1 activities, partner parliaments of graduated countries, EUMSP, Partner focal points, EUD staff, and members and close collaborators of the Community of Practice.Unit of Measure: Percentage of respondents who reply either Yes (to a large extent) or Yes (to some extent).Disaggregation: None required. For learning purposes, the survey will collect data on respondents Gender (Female, Male, Other, Prefer Not to Say), Country (Partner Parliaments disaggregation, EUMSPs) and Type of Participant (Parliamentary staff, member of Parliament, official / staff of the European Union, Scholar, and other)Known Data Limitations: the data is subject to bias as it is based on respondent perceptions, it may also be imprecise as individuals perceptions of the degree of change regarding parliamentary development may vary.Data Source and Plan for Collection: One annual survey: Core Partners Annual SurveyMethod of Data Collection and Construction: Respondents will be asked the same question According to you, have the INTER PARES activities been effective in strengthening parliamentary development? And will respond with one of four choices: Yes (to a large extent) Yes (to some extent) No Not sure. Follow up questions will explore the reason for the choice. Information will be collected from survey, with responses collected on a data sheet. The percent of respondents saying either Yes (to a large extent) or Yes (to some extent), among the total number of responses will be calculated and recorded as a percentage. Person responsible for data collection: INTER PARES project and M&E team through surveys.Baseline: This item did not exist prior to the start of the project; hence the baseline is zero.

description.narrative: Measures the number of policy/process changes partners are instituting in the priority areas the project is working on. Changes indicate progress to project outcomes. By interviewing our partners (boundary partners) the project will seek to identify both moderate or incremental and more substantial institutional changes that contribute to enhancing how our partners may be changing to work on such issues. Understanding what milestones are in fact made will demonstrate both the projects contribution to outcome two, but by looking at incremental steps as well as more institutionalized changes, will help the project to monitor progress that partners are making. Information will be used during implementation to monitor progress and make any necessary changes and the data will also be used to assess the achievement of the outcomes regarding enhancing EU engagement with parliamentary development.Precise Definition of terms: This indicator counts the number of new changes in the behaviour, relationships, and or practices of an individual, group, or organization the project partners and collaborators, related to the cross cutting themes. The changes can be moderate (small, or incremental changes) or major institutional/policy changes that have the potential to contribute to impact level changes, may be counted. Both expected changes and unanticipated changes may be counted.a)behaviors If actors, partners, collaborators, members of the COP, EUDs, EUMSPs, and other collaborators and partners change the ways they behave, through observable actions or activities. This may be counted. In parliaments MPs might start to request more information on the issues. Or they might hold more consultations with citizens, publish more on social media regarding the topic, discuss the issues more in plenary debate.b)relationships: new ways that individuals and partners interact. For example, a committee chair consults other committee colleagues more frequently about issues, or committees start to coordinate differently with professional staff on the issues, or relationships among the community of practice show changes, or between EUMSPs and partners, etc. For example, new partnerships and collaborations may arise around specific crosscutting themes, the COP partners might develop new relations with partner or EUMSP parliaments, the EUD participants might change relations with the parliament,c)practices: the application of a new method /ways of working, which can include small steps or a series of steps related to addressing the themes b procedures: (i.e. a series of steps followed in a regular order representing the official process for carrying out a task or function) , c mechanisms: (a technique used to carry out a task or process, e.g., new consultations in committees to discuss one of the themes with citizens, ), d tools: (an instrument used to carry out a task or function, like a guideline or manual with instructions for completing a task, a manual for the review of legislation using gendersensitive considerations definitions for a d may overlap but each new element may only be counted once, developed through the project and in relation to the project themes. New policies can also be counted.

title.narrative: 2.1. Number of changes taken to establish new behaviours, relationships orpractices for effective action on cross cutting themes by EUMSPs or Partner Parliaments

description.narrative: Management Purpose: Measures the number of policy/process changes partners are instituting in the priority areas the project is working on. Changes indicate progress to project outcomes. By interviewing our partners (boundary partners) the project will seek to identify both moderate or incremental and more substantial institutional changes that contribute to enhancing how our partners may be changing to work on such issues. Understanding what milestones are in fact made will demonstrate both the projects contribution to outcome two, but by looking at incremental steps as well as more institutionalized changes, will help the project to monitor progress that partners are making. Information will be used during implementation to monitor progress and make any necessary changes and the data will also be used to assess the achievement of the outcomes regarding enhancing EU engagement with parliamentary development. Precise Definition of terms: This indicator counts the number of new changes in the behaviour, relationships, and or practices of an individual, group, or organization the project partners and collaborators, related to the cross cutting themes. The changes can be moderate (small, or incremental changes) or major institutional/policy changes that have the potential to contribute to impact level changes. Both expected changes and unanticipated changes may be counted.a)Behaviors: If actors, partners, collaborators, members of the COP, EUDs, EUMSPs, partner parliaments under outcome 3 and other collaborators and partners change the ways they behave, through observable actions or activities. This may be counted. In parliaments MPs might start to request more information on the issues. Or they might hold more consultations with citizens, publish more on social media regarding the topic, discuss the issues more in plenary debate. b)Relationships: new ways that individuals and partners interact. For example, a committee chair consults other committee colleagues more frequently about issues, or committees start to coordinate differently with professional staff on the issues, or relationships among the community of practice show changes, or between EUMSPs and partners, etc. For example, new partnerships and collaborations may arise around specific cross cutting themes, the COP partners might develop new relations with partner or EUMSP parliaments, the EUD participants might change relations with the parliament,c)a Practices: the application of a new method /ways of working, which can include small steps or a series of steps related to addressing the themes. b procedures: (i.e. a series of steps followed in a regular order representing the official process for carrying out a task or function) , c mechanisms: (a technique used to carry out a task or process, e.g., new consultations in committees to discuss one of the themes with citizens, ), d tools: (an instrument used to carry out a task or function, like a guideline or manual with instructions for completing a task, a manual for the review of legislation using gendersensitive considerations definitions for a d may overlap but each new element may only be counted once, developed through the project and in relation to the project themes. New policies can also be counted.Unit of Measure: Number, (integer) of changes across partners which are summed up into one number for the indicator. Disaggregated by: None required, however for narrative reporting the project will count and analyze the changes per theme and type of change (moderate/major). title.narrative: 3.2. Number of changes taken to establish new behaviours, relationships or practices towards more effective parliamentary functions by partner parliaments

description.narrative: Management Purpose definition: Measures the number of policy/process changes partner parliaments are instituting in the priority areas the project is working on. Changes indicate progress to project outcomes. By interviewing our partners (the project will seek to identify both moderate or incremental and more substantial institutional changes that contribute to enhancing how our partners may be changing to work on such issues. Understanding what milestones are in fact made will demonstrate both the projects contribution to outcome three, but by looking at incremental steps as well as more institutionalized changes, will help the project to monitor progress that partners are making. Information will be used during implementation to monitor progress and make any necessary changes and the data will also be used to assess the achievement of the outcomes regarding enhancing EU engagement with parliamentary development. Precise Definition: This indicator counts the number of new changes in the behaviour, relationships, and or practices of partner parliaments. The changes can be moderate (small, or incremental changes) or major institutional/policy changes that have the potential to contribute to impact level changes, may be counted. Both expected changes and unanticipated changes may be counted.a)behaviors: If partner parliaments partners change the ways they behave, through observable actions or activities. This may be counted. In parliaments MPs might start to request more information on the issues. Or they might hold more consultations with citizens, publish more on social media regarding the topic, discuss the issues more in plenary debate.b)relationships: new ways that partner parliaments interact. For example, a committee chair consults other committee colleagues more frequently about issues, or committees start to coordinate differently with professional staff on the issues, or relationships among the community of practice show changes, or between EUMSPs and partners, etc. For example, new partnerships and collaborations may arise around specific crosscutting themes, the COP partners might develop new relations with partner or EUMSP parliaments, the EUD participants might change relations with the parliament,c)practices: the application of a new method /ways of working, which can include small steps or a series of steps related to addressing the themes. b procedures: (i.e. a series of steps followed in a regular order representing the official process for carrying out a task or function) , c mechanisms: (a technique used to carry out a task or process, e.g., new consultations in committees to discuss one of the themes with citizens, ), d tools: (an instrument used to carry out a task or function, like a guideline or manual with instructions for completing a task, a manual for the review of legislation using gendersensitive considerations definitions for a d may overlap but each new element may only be counted once, developed through the project and in relation to the project themes. New policies can also be counted.Known Data Limitations: potential for informant bias. INTER PARES can contribute to a change but not see the results within the time of the partnership.

description.narrative: The Bertelsmann Transformation Index (BTI) analyses and evaluates the quality of democracy, a market economy and political management in 129 developing and transition countries. It measures successes and setbacks on the path toward a democracy based on the rule of law and a socially responsible market economy. The BTI Status Index ranks countries according to their quality of democracy and market economy as of January 31, 2015. The state of political transformation is measured in terms of five criteria (Stateness, Political participation; Rule of Law; Stability of democratic institutions; Political and social integration), which in turn are derived from assessments made in response to 18 questions. Political participation is measured by the normative statement: The populace decides who rules and it has other political freedoms.Thresholds determine five categories:Excellent (8.50 10.00); Sound (6.50 8.49); Fair (4.50 6.49); Flawed (2.50 4.49); Poor (1.00 2.49)More detail on the concepts used can be found here https://btiproject.org/en/?&cb00000

title.narrative: Country score on the Economist Intelligence Units Democracy Index

description.narrative: The Democracy Index is based on five categories: electoral process and pluralism; civil liberties; the functioning of government; political participation; and political culture. It provides a snapshot of the state of democracy for 165 independent states, which make up the majority of the worlds states (microstates are excluded). There is both an overall score as well as scores in individual categories. Based on their scores on a range of indicators within these categories, each country is then itself categorised as one of four types of regime: full democracies; flawed democracies; hybrid regimes; and authoritarian regimes.

comment.narrative: No quantitative target will be established current values will be tracked.
